text:
maria (sales): Ping — Acme POC reporting auth errors when calling /v1/generate. They get 403 "org_mismatch". Can someone help? (cc @sam)

acme-poc (customer): Hey team, we rolled a new API key yesterday and now calls fail with {"error":"invalid_org","message":"key belongs to org: acme-staging"}

sam (solutions): Thanks. Do you have the full curl you're running? Also paste the header from the failing response.

acme-poc (customer): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-x","input":"hello"}'

acme-poc (customer): Response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"invalid_org","detail":"key org mismatch: expected acme-prod"}

sam (solutions): Looks like the key is scoped to acme-staging but their project is in acme-prod. Two quick fixes: (1) create a new API key under acme-prod OR (2) bind the existing key to project using the console - but binding requires owner perms. Which do you prefer?

maria (sales): Customer asked for minimal change — prefer issuing new key under acme-prod. Also flagged in contract that POC uses prod org for load testing. Any docs I can send them?

sam (solutions): Use Console -> Team Settings -> API Keys -> Create key. Make sure to select "Project: acme-prod" and enable scopes: "inference:generate" and "inference:stream". Example curl for token test:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/whoami
# returns {"org":"acme-prod","scopes":["inference:generate"]}

acme-poc (customer): Also: our infra rotates keys nightly. Is there a way to do key rotation without downtime? We hit rate limits when new key starts.

sam (solutions): Yes — implement dual-key warmup: keep old key active until new key validated, then revoke. Alternatively use the service account pattern + short-lived tokens via KMS integration. I'll draft steps.

alex (security): Quick note — if you plan to automate rotation, ensure KMS is used and update SQS secrets with versioning. Also we'll need to sign the security questionnaire Q4 (asked about key rotation policy). Maria, can you attach the questionnaire here?

maria (sales): attaching now (link to doc) — customer wants to confirm rotation SLA and key isolation per environment.

sam (solutions): I'll add a sample policy and a small script to perform warm swap. Pasting psuedo steps:

1) create new key in acme-prod
2) deploy to service account env var NEW_KEY
3) hit /v1/keys/whoami to verify org
4) run smoke tests for 10k requests or 5 minutes
5) update traffic router to prefer NEW_KEY
6) revoke old key

acme-poc (customer): We tried step 3 but whoami returned acme-staging for new key as well. Could there be a bug in console creating keys in wrong org?

sam (solutions): Uh — that's odd. Please paste the console screenshot and the key id (last 6 chars). I'll check server logs. @deploy-bot can you pull auth logs for key ending ...C12345 between 2025-12-14T09:00:00Z and 2025-12-14T10:00:00Z?

deploy-bot: (automated) auth_logs pulled: key=C12345 -> created_by=maria; created_org=acme-staging; console_org_selection=acme-prod? (inconsistent entry)

sam (solutions): Found the issue: console selection dropdown had a stale cache bug where the form showed acme-prod but backend created under acme-staging. We've deployed a fix. For immediate workaround, I'll create a new key directly via our internal API in acme-prod and paste it here.

sam (solutions): Created new key sk_prod_78XYZ (partial) for acme-prod. Please test.

acme-poc (customer): Tested — whoami returns acme-prod. Generate OK. :tada:

maria (sales): Awesome. I'll update customer and note this as a known console bug. Any follow-ups for security questionnaire?

alex (security): Please add rotation cadence and KMS flow to the doc; we'll sign once updated.

maria (sales): Will do. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
